task: Identify the most recent development or update in Brexit negotiations as reported on BBC News and report the key points and any stated impacts on European economies.
answer: Most recent Brexit negotiation development on BBC News: 'Burnham to push for new post-Brexit deals at EU summit' (dated 12 October 2026, URL https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cqev3xvejyvjo). Key points: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told MPs he will push for new post-Brexit deals with the EU at a summit in November, seeking deeper cooperation on youth mobility, food and drink, and energy to drive UK economic growth. He warned the EU's 'Made In Europe' plans pose a risk to UK manufacturing and said he is in talks for an arrangement that works for the UK. Labour's manifesto red lines (no return to the single market, customs union, or freedom of movement) remain until the next election. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused him of 'unpicking' the deal the UK signed with the EU. Impacts on European economies: Burnham claimed the agreements could add the equivalent of £10bn per year to the UK economy by 2040; a food deal could reverse damage from border checks (Scottish salmon faces 100% document checks costing ~£100m in lost exports); an energy deal involving emissions trading could lower energy costs for households and businesses, cutting wholesale energy costs by 20% in Northern Ireland; and the EU's 'Made In Europe' proposals, aimed at protecting EU industry from Chinese competitors, could impact British industry and supply chains.
